neighbours.label: The lone space token that the tokenizer splits off by itself, mid-sentence: the space in front of a number written in digits (e.g. 'hikers counted| |27 deer'), or the extra space of a double space between words ('the  garden'). Quiet on numbers spelled out in words, on '$5'-style amounts (the space merges into the symbol), and on text with single spaces only.
neighbours.short: lone space token (before digits, or double space)
fire: The hikers counted 27 deer along the ridge before noon.
She planted tomatoes in the  garden behind the shed.
Our train leaves at platform 9 in about ten minutes.
The recipe calls for 3 eggs and a cup of flour.
He walked  slowly toward the old lighthouse.
There were 450 people waiting outside the stadium.
The library closes early on  Sundays during the summer.
We drove 120 miles before stopping for lunch.
quiet: The hikers counted twenty-seven deer along the ridge before noon.
Our train leaves at platform nine in about ten minutes.
The recipe calls for three eggs and a cup of flour.
Tickets cost $45 for people waiting outside the stadium.
We drove a hundred and twenty miles before stopping for lunch.
My grandmother turned ninety-two last spring and still bakes bread.
The cat jumped onto the windowsill and fell asleep.
The snack at the end of the hallway costs $3 now.

Exploration: the score at the space is set by the preceding words, not the following token (' the 90th' and ' the  ninetieth' scored identically).
